title: Reported Speech
content:
Definition

English: Reported speech (or indirect speech) is when someone’s words are reported in a different form rather than quoting them exactly.
Hindi: Reported speech (ya paroksh vachan) tab hota hai jab kisi ke shabd sidhe na batakar alag roop mein vyakt kiye jate hain.

It contrasts with direct speech, which uses exact words in quotes.
Yeh sidhe vachan se alag hai, jo shabdon ko quotes mein bilkul waisa hi batata hai.

Example: Direct: She said, 'I am tired.' Indirect: She said that she was tired.
Hindi: Direct: Usne kaha, 'Main thak gayi hoon.' Indirect: Usne kaha ki woh thak gayi thi.

title: Rules for Changing Direct to Indirect Speech
content:
Guidelines

English: To convert direct speech to indirect: 1) Remove quotation marks, 2) Change pronouns as needed, 3) Adjust verb tense (usually one step back), 4) Change time/place expressions, 5) Use 'that' or other conjunctions if needed.
Hindi: Sidhe vachan ko paroksh mein badalne ke niyam: 1) Quotation marks hatao, 2) Sarvanam ko zarurat ke hisaab se badlo, 3) Kriya ka tense ek kadam peechhe karo, 4) Samay/sthan ke shabd badlo, 5) 'Ki' ya doosre samuchchay bodhak ka prayog karo agar zaruri ho.

Example: Direct: He said, 'I will come tomorrow.' Indirect: He said that he would come the next day.
Hindi: Direct: Usne kaha, 'Main kal aaunga.' Indirect: Usne kaha ki woh agle din aayega.

title: Tense Changes in Reported Speech
content:
Explanation

English: Verb tenses in direct speech usually shift back one tense in reported speech (e.g., present to past, past to past perfect).
Hindi: Sidhe vachan mein kriya ka tense paroksh vachan mein ek tense peechhe chala jata hai (jaise, vartamaan se bhoot, bhoot se poorna bhoot).

Tense Shift Examples

  • Present Simple: Direct: 'I play.' Indirect: He said that he played.
    Hindi: Direct: 'Main khelta hoon.' Indirect: Usne kaha ki woh khelta tha.
  • Past Simple: Direct: 'I ate.' Indirect: She said that she had eaten.
    Hindi: Direct: 'Maine khaya.' Indirect: Usne kaha ki usne khaya tha.
  • Present Continuous: Direct: 'I am reading.' Indirect: He said that he was reading.
    Hindi: Direct: 'Main padh raha hoon.' Indirect: Usne kaha ki woh padh raha tha.
  • Will: Direct: 'I will go.' Indirect: She said that she would go.
    Hindi: Direct: 'Main jaunga.' Indirect: Usne kaha ki woh jayegi.
Example: Direct: 'I have finished.' Indirect: He said that he had finished.
Hindi: Direct: 'Maine pura kar liya.' Indirect: Usne kaha ki usne pura kar liya tha.

title: Pronoun Changes in Reported Speech
content:
Use

English: Pronouns change based on the speaker and listener in the reported form to reflect the new context.
Hindi: Sarvanam bolne wale aur sunne wale ke anusaar paroksh roop mein badalte hain taaki naya sandarbh vyakt ho.

Example: Direct: She said, 'I am happy.' Indirect: She said that she was happy.
Hindi: Direct: Usne kaha, 'Main khush hoon.' Indirect: Usne kaha ki woh khush thi.

title: Time and Place Expression Changes
content:
Explanation

English: Time and place words change in reported speech to match the new context (e.g., 'now' becomes 'then,' 'today' becomes 'that day').
Hindi: Samay aur sthan ke shabd paroksh vachan mein naye sandarbh ke anusaar badalte hain (jaise, 'abhi' ban jata hai 'tab,' 'aaj' ban jata hai 'us din').

Examples

  • 'Now' → 'Then' (Abhi → Tab)
  • 'Today' → 'That day' (Aaj → Us din)
  • 'Tomorrow' → 'The next day' (Kal → Agla din)
  • 'Here' → 'There' (Yahan → Wahan)
Example: Direct: 'I’ll meet you here tomorrow.' Indirect: He said that he would meet me there the next day.
Hindi: Direct: 'Main tumse yahan kal milunga.' Indirect: Usne kaha ki woh mujhse wahan agle din milega.

title: Reported Questions
content:
Use

English: Questions in direct speech become statements in reported speech, using 'if/whether' for yes/no questions or question words (who, what, etc.) for wh-questions.
Hindi: Sidhe vachan ke prashn paroksh vachan mein vakya ban jate hain, haan/na prashnon ke liye 'ki' ya 'kya,' aur wh-prashnon ke liye prashn shabd (kaun, kya, aadi) ka prayog hota hai.

Structure

Subject + Asked/Wondered + If/Whether/Question Word + Clause

Example: Direct: 'Are you coming?' Indirect: He asked if I was coming.
Hindi: Direct: 'Kya tum aa rahe ho?' Indirect: Usne poochha ki kya main aa raha tha.

title: Reported Commands and Requests
content:
Use

English: Commands and requests in direct speech use 'to' + verb or phrases like 'asked to' or 'told to' in reported speech.
Hindi: Sidhe vachan ke aadesh ya anurodh paroksh vachan mein 'ko' + kriya ya 'poochha' ya 'kaha' jaise shabdon ke saath badalte hain.

Structure

Subject + Told/Asked + Object + to + Verb

Example: Direct: 'Close the door.' Indirect: He told me to close the door.
Hindi: Direct: 'Darwaza band karo.' Indirect: Usne mujhe darwaza band karne ko kaha.

title: Special Cases in Reported Speech
content:
Explanation

English: Some situations don’t require tense changes, like universal truths, or when the reporting verb is in the present tense. Modal verbs like 'would,' 'could,' or 'might' often remain unchanged.
Hindi: Kuch sthitiyon mein tense nahi badalta, jaise vishwa satya, ya jab reporting verb vartamaan kaal mein ho. Modal verbs jaise 'would,' 'could,' ya 'might' aksar bina badle rehte hain.

Examples:
  • Direct: 'The sun rises in the east.' Indirect: He said that the sun rises in the east.
    Hindi: Direct: 'Suraj poorab mein ugta hai.' Indirect: Usne kaha ki suraj poorab mein ugta hai.
  • Direct: 'I might go.' Indirect: She says that she might go.
    Hindi: Direct: 'Main ja sakta hoon.' Indirect: Woh kehti hai ki woh ja sakti hai.
